members.name: nameNotResolved
members.doc:
The host (or proxy) name did not resolve. Separated from the other
transport failures because it is the one that usually means the URL is
wrong rather than the network being down, and a caller that retries on
a schedule wants to treat the two differently.

types.name: HttpClient
types.doc:
Minimal libcurl-backed client. Each call owns its own easy handle, so the
static methods are safe to call from multiple threads concurrently.

members.name: GlobalInit
members.doc:
Process-wide curl init/teardown. Idempotent; the request methods call
GlobalInit() lazily, so explicit use is optional.

members.name: Post
members.signature: static HttpResponse Post(const std::string& url, const std::string& body, const std::vector<std::string>& headers = {}, long timeoutSeconds = 15)
members.doc: POST a raw string body.

members.name: Request
members.signature: static HttpResponse Request(const std::string& method, const std::string& url, const std::string& body = "", const std::vector<std::string>& headers = {}, long timeoutSeconds = 15)
members.doc:
Any HTTP verb ("GET", "POST", "PUT", "PATCH", "DELETE", ...). An empty
body sends no payload; GET with a body is refused by construction (a
body on GET is undefined per RFC 9110 and proxies drop it silently).

types.name: ECrashFlushMode
types.doc:
Who is asking for the upload, which decides what a game's crash settings
(FCrashReportClientSettings, read from each report's .txt) let through.

members.name: NextLaunch
members.doc:
A launch: reports the player agreed to upfront, plus every report no
game configured (the editor, engine tools).

members.name: UserConsented
members.doc: The reporter's Send button — the player has just agreed.

members.name: Unattended
members.doc: The watchdog with no window: only a game that sends unattended.

types.name: FCrashUploadQueueStatus
types.doc:
What is waiting in the crash dir and what the last tries of the default
endpoint ran into, read from disk, so any process can show it.

members.name: FlushPending
members.doc:
Scan the crash dir for *.dmp, POST each (with its .txt sidecar) to the
Sentry minidump endpoint, and delete on success. No-op (returns 0) if
no DSN is configured or no dumps exist. Failed uploads are LEFT on
disk for the next run, so it's safe to call when offline.

DSN resolution, per report: the report_dsn line its .txt carries (the
game's [CrashReportClient] Dsn), else explicit SetDsn(), else the DSN
compiled into SentryCrashUploader.cpp. A report its game disabled, or
one `mode` may not send without asking, is left on disk.
Returns the number of reports successfully uploaded.

Synchronous, but the common case (no pending dumps) is just a cheap
directory scan. Only does network I/O when a crash actually happened.

members.name: FlushPending
members.signature: static int FlushPending(ECrashFlushMode mode, const std::string& onlyBasePath = std::string())
members.doc:
`onlyBasePath` (a report path without extension) limits the flush to
that one report — what the reporter's Send button consents to.

members.name: SetDsn
members.doc:
Provide the fallback DSN explicitly (overrides the compiled one) for
reports that carry none. Empty restores the compiled one.

members.name: GetLastEndpoint
members.doc:
The minidump endpoint the last FlushPending() on THIS thread posted to
(or would have, had it not been backing off). Empty when it tried none.

members.name: GetLastWithheldCount
members.doc:
Reports the last FlushPending() on THIS thread left on disk because
their game's settings did not allow sending them in that mode.

members.name: SetCrashDir
members.doc: Override the scan dir (default <state root>/<Product>/Saved/Crashes).

members.name: GetLastError
members.doc:
Human-readable reason the last FlushPending() on THIS thread failed to
upload a report (HTTP status + server body, or the transport error).
Empty when every report went through.

members.name: AreRetriesSuppressed
members.doc:
True when the last FlushPending() on THIS thread stopped retrying the
configured endpoint because its host has not resolved for several runs.
A UI that promises "retried on the next launch" must not say so then —
nothing will be retried until the DSN is corrected or a day passes.

members.name: GetQueueStatus
members.doc:
The queue in the crash dir against the endpoint reports without a DSN
of their own go to. Reports stay queued until an upload succeeds.

members.name: DescribeQueueStatus
members.doc:
One sentence for a person: how many reports wait and why, or empty when
nothing is queued.
